runs.note:
HPI/Care History:
36 year old male, Tear of posterior cruciate ligament, right knee, Grade II (conservative management), IE 04/23/2026.

Clinical Summary:
PN 06/11/2026 (IE 04/23/2026): 14 VTD. Pain 2/10 with stair descent; 0/10 at rest (5/10 with stair descent, 2/10 at rest). PT ROM: Right knee flexion 125° (95°), Right knee extension 0° (-5°). MMT: Right quadriceps 4/5 (3+/5), Right hamstrings 4+/5 (4/5), Left quadriceps 5/5. LEFS 58/80 (36/80). Special tests: Posterior drawer Grade I laxity right with firm end feel, Posterior sag sign trace positive right. 1/4 LTGs met.

POC:
2x/week × 4 weeks

Requested Visits:
8

Determination and Rationale:
Partial Denial — Taper Indicated: Patient has received 14 visits with measurable progress across pain (2/10 with stairs, 0/10 at rest, improved from baseline 5/10 and 2/10), range of motion (flexion 125° vs baseline 95°, now within 10° of the 135° functional norm; extension 0° vs baseline -5°, now full), and strength (quadriceps 4/5 vs baseline 3+/5, hamstrings 4+/5 vs baseline 4/5) — all now representing mild residual deficits. LEFS has improved from 36/80 to 58/80, exceeding the published MCID. Given the substantial visits already delivered (14) and mild remaining deficits in pain, ROM, and strength with documented progress, continued high-frequency skilled care at the requested 2x/week for 8 visits is not supported; a taper toward discharge is indicated instead. Approved 4 visits at 1x/week over 4 weeks to consolidate gains, progress the home exercise program, and address residual return-to-sport limitations (single-leg/cutting difficulty, rail-assisted stair descent, mild dynamic valgus, 11% Y-Balance asymmetry) prior to discharge. Benchmark applied: typical episode of care approximately 18 visits (upper bound ~24) referencing the JOSPT Knee Ligament Sprain CPG (Logerstedt et al., 2017) as the closest available analogous guideline, since no PCL-specific CPG exists.

Approved Visits:
4
